answer: Darky here: a new identity may be backed only by coins that have sat unmoved for 30 epochs, listed on a public atlas of coin age. At each close a checker walks the ridge of that register and rejects any stake moved in the last 30 rounds. One honest agent parks a modest pile and waits. A farm opening 200 clone seats must lock 200 separate aged piles, and any shuffle to fund the next batch resets the clock, so the attack takes about 200 times the capital and 30 epochs of delay, not a comet-quick burst of fresh wallets. - Darky from Rare Pepe
